## **INTERVIEW GUIDE** {#interview-guide}

**Interviewee:** Kitchen406 Owner  
**Business:** Kitchen406  
**Purpose:** To gather detailed information about the bakery's existing operations, challenges, business requirements, and expectations for the proposed system.

**Business Background and Daily Operations**

Kitchen406 began operating in December 2020, initially producing orders only during the November–December Christmas season. The business launched its Facebook page in February 2026\. The owner previously worked as an HVAC engineer for 22 years before leaving the profession in 2025 to pursue culinary studies, which she completed in December 2025\. Her sister and business partner also left her employment in early 2026\. The bakery is now their full-time occupation.

Both owners share operational responsibilities, although the co-owner commonly promotes products through her personal social media accounts. The owner's daughter occasionally assists with minor tasks, such as folding cake boxes and decorating cupcakes. Baking generally begins at 9:00 AM, while operating days depend on incoming orders. Orders may be temporarily suspended during vacations or food conventions.

The bakery aims to receive 20–30 orders monthly, but demand fluctuates significantly. The previous month recorded seven orders, while only two custom cakes had been booked at the beginning of August. During busy months such as June, the bakery handles approximately five orders weekly. Christmas is the busiest season, with the previous Christmas generating sales of 300 brownie boxes and 200 fruitcakes. Other periods of increased demand include Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, Father's Day, and the beginning of the school year.

Most customers are repeat buyers, relatives, friends, or referrals. The bakery has not formally rejected orders but offers available alternatives when requested products cannot be completed within the required time. Custom cakes consume the most time, particularly when relatives request them with only one day's notice. Despite these challenges, the owners enjoy contributing to customers' celebrations and are satisfied with their current baking activities.

Their long-term goal is to operate daily, producing two to three custom cakes weekly and approximately 30–40 bread and pastry orders monthly.

**Products and Menu**

Kitchen406 offers breads, pastries, and customized cakes. All standard products are sold in boxes containing six or twelve pieces, with mixed flavors generally offered only during Christmas. The owners are reviewing competitor prices and intend to finalize a smaller product menu to simplify inventory management. The complete price list and ingredient information have not yet been finalized.

Custom cakes are currently available in 6-inch and 9-inch sizes, with two cake layers rather than multiple tiers. Customers may choose vanilla or chocolate cake, buttercream or chocolate ganache icing, and round or heart-shaped designs. Cake colors can be customized using customer-provided reference photographs. Additional decorations may be free or charged separately depending on the request. More cake sizes may be introduced in the future.

Allergen information has been considered but is not routinely requested by customers. The owner has previously included allergy information when preparing pastries for school gatherings.

Product catalogs are shared through menu photographs or Facebook page links, although the page is not regularly updated. Existing product photographs are available for the developers.

The initial subscription products identified were burger buns, dinner rolls, sandwich bread, meat buns, Spanish bread, banana muffins, and chocolate chip muffins. Sourdough bread may be added later. Each subscription product has a designated weekly delivery day, with enrollment required one week before the first scheduled delivery.

**How Customers Find and Reach the Business**

Customers discover Kitchen406 through Facebook, Instagram, and referrals from friends or acquaintances. The business maintains a Facebook page but does not post regularly.

The owner typically responds immediately to customer inquiries when available. However, messages are not attended to during baking to avoid distractions. Inquiries received outside working hours are answered when convenient.

The bakery has not lost orders because of delayed or missed messages. However, many inquiries do not result in purchases, which the owner attributes partly to the high number of competing Facebook sellers.

**Standard Order Intake**

Standard orders are recorded manually on a whiteboard and in Google Sheets. The bakery collects customers' names, contact numbers, and delivery addresses, with contact numbers required even when communication occurs through Messenger.

The owner suggested accepting up to four different product orders daily or up to ten orders when producing a single item, excluding custom cakes. The bakery has not experienced accepting more orders than it can fulfill. Advance notice of approximately one week is preferred when blocking unavailable dates.

No established policy currently governs corrections to finalized orders. The owner indicated that mistakes involving quantities, addresses, or other details would be handled through discussion and negotiation.

**Custom Cake Requests**

Custom cake requests are primarily assessed through customer-provided reference photographs. The owners can generally determine feasibility immediately after viewing the design. Requests involving overly complex designs are addressed by suggesting achievable alternatives rather than directly rejecting customers.

Custom cake prices start at ₱1,350. The base 6-inch cake includes two layers with filling, a choice of vanilla or chocolate flavor, buttercream or chocolate ganache icing, and basic decorations such as sprinkles. Additional themed elements, including acrylic toppers, shaped chocolates, and decorative toys, may add approximately ₱300–₱500 depending on complexity.

Prices are generally fixed, although complimentary toppers may be offered. The owners previously experienced underpricing custom cakes and treated the resulting losses as learning experiences.

Custom cake requests require at least three days' advance notice, although earlier reservations are preferred. Customers commonly place birthday cake orders weeks in advance. Production capacity is approximately two custom cakes weekly.

The owners have not encountered complaints involving finished cakes failing to meet expectations. For simultaneous deliveries in different locations, trusted family members may assist with transportation.

**Pricing, Fees, Discounts, and Promotions**

Ingredient costs typically include an additional 5–10% allowance to account for price fluctuations. Product markups are percentage-based, with competitor prices considered when determining selling prices. However, the owners avoid frequent price changes to maintain customer relationships and competitiveness.

Formal discounts are uncommon. Instead, customers may receive complimentary muffins, brownies, or decorative toppers. Free delivery may occasionally be offered for high-volume orders or valued customers.

Custom cakes are currently delivered without additional fees. Delivery charges for standard orders are generally paid separately to the courier. The bakery has not experienced customer complaints or confusion regarding its existing charges.

**Payments**

Customers currently pay upon delivery, and cash on delivery is accepted for all order types. When digital payments are made, customers submit screenshots through Messenger as proof of payment. The owners verify payments immediately and have not encountered fraudulent payment confirmations.

Acknowledgment receipts are issued after payment, while daily sales transactions are recorded in Google Sheets.

**Scheduling, Capacity, and Production**

Production is planned the day before baking, with items requiring the longest preparation time prioritized. The schedule varies according to demand and is not consistently filled a fixed number of days in advance.

Baking begins at approximately 9:00 AM and ends when production is completed. During Christmas, work may continue until nighttime. Standard products generally require a few hours, although bread preparation takes longer because of proofing. Custom cakes typically require two days of preparation, while custom cakes and sourdough bread are among the most time-consuming products.

Most products are prepared the day before fulfillment to allow sufficient cooling and packaging time. Orders containing similar products are produced in batches to reduce oven fuel consumption and preparation time.

The bakery has not experienced delayed deliveries. During periods of high demand, the owners plan production and delivery schedules in advance.

**Fulfillment: Pickup and Delivery**

Customers collect pickup orders directly from the bakery and usually specify their preferred pickup time, which the owners accommodate. Missed pickups have not occurred, although some customers arrive late.

For standard deliveries, the owners book the courier and relay the customer's delivery information. Custom cakes are delivered personally, with delivery routes and schedules planned in advance. Customers are notified immediately before the owners leave the kitchen, particularly for deliveries to event venues with specific arrival requirements.

Delivery failures, incorrect addresses, and transit damage have not been experienced. The owners prioritize secure packaging and manually confirm that customers have received their orders.

**After the Order**

The owners request customer feedback, which commonly arrives through photographs or videos. Customer information and previous orders are retained for reference.

Complaints are handled according to their circumstances, with possible refunds or discounts considered. Customers may cancel custom cake orders at least three days before fulfillment and standard orders at least one day before fulfillment.

No formal refund policy has been established because the business has not experienced refunded cancellations. The bakery also maintains no formal list of customers prohibited from ordering, although the owner may personally remember difficult transactions.

**Record Keeping and Business Numbers**

Kitchen406 records sales and expenses, including ingredients, packaging, utilities, maintenance, and equipment repairs, in Google Sheets. Profitability is calculated monthly by subtracting total expenses from total sales rather than tracking exact profit for each product.

Ingredients are purchased in bulk to reduce costs, and existing stock is monitored regularly. Restocking generally occurs when supplies are nearly depleted, with shipping lead times considered for ingredients sourced outside Cebu.

Purchasing frequency depends on order volume. The owners actively seek suppliers and attend food conventions to compare available brands and ingredients.

The owner expressed interest in more accessible information regarding monthly income and the bakery's busiest operating days.

**People Who Will Use the System**

The owners prefer restricting staff access to specific operational functions rather than allowing access to all business information. Either owner can independently handle bakery operations when the other is unavailable.

The bakery generally has reliable internet connectivity. In the event of an outage, the owners would use mobile data or seek an alternative connection to continue operating.

**Expectations for the Proposed System**

The owner confirmed that payment is required before production begins. After preparation, the bakery schedules delivery and notifies the customer when the order is ready. The owner initially described payment occurring after delivery.

The owner initially preferred allowing first-time customers to order as guests while requiring repeat customers to register. Desired features include new-order notifications, customer-accessible order tracking, and optional order-history and reordering functions.

Custom cake discussions should remain personally handled because of their individualized requirements. When asked to identify three essential features, the owner prioritized order notifications, ingredient inventory monitoring, and monthly sales or income summaries.

No specific website was identified as a design reference. The owner also expressed an expectation that the system should contribute to increasing business sales.

**Admin Dashboard Needs**

The owner wants the dashboard to immediately display incoming orders. Requested management features include daily preparation lists, an order calendar showing upcoming and blocked dates, and status labels such as paid, preparing, ready, and delivered.

Automated pricing suggestions were considered useful but not essential because competitive market conditions prevent immediate price adjustments. The owners prefer purchasing ingredients in bulk to reduce the impact of price increases.

Temporarily unavailable products should remain visible in the catalog but be marked as sold out.

**Concerns, Limitations, and Risks**

The owner's primary concern is customer adoption, particularly among senior citizens who make up a significant portion of the bakery's existing customers. Some may be reluctant to use websites or applications, although other customers may adopt the platform if it is easy to navigate.

The owner is comfortable storing customer names, contact numbers, and addresses in the system but has not established specific restrictions regarding which business or personal information should remain private.

The bakery's recipes were identified as information and practices that must remain unchanged.

**Timeline and Success**

The owner has not imposed a development deadline and is willing to adopt the system once it is completed. The developers were given flexibility to establish the project timeline.

Approximately six to seven hours weekly are currently spent answering inquiries and organizing orders. The owner also confirmed availability to participate in system testing and provide feedback before deployment.

**Additional Information**

The owner indicated that the questionnaire adequately covered the bakery's operations and had no further information to add.

No similar system has previously been developed for Kitchen406. The owner also reported having no acquaintances or fellow bakers whose experiences with online management systems could be used as references.

**Gaps in the Documented Process**

Order availability is checked immediately upon receiving a customer inquiry. If the requested date is unavailable, the customer is informed that the bakery cannot fulfill the order on that date.

If a payment cannot be verified through the bank or e-wallet, the owner contacts the customer directly. No policy exists for abandoned or unpaid orders because customers currently pay after delivery.

Custom cakes are personally delivered by the owners. Existing orders do not have assigned reference numbers and are identified using customer names. The owner is open to introducing order numbers as transaction volume increases.

**Subscriptions**

The proposed subscription program originated from the owner's sister and business partner rather than from existing customer requests. Initial offerings include burger buns, dinner rolls, Spanish bread, meat buns, sandwich bread, and muffins.

Subscriptions consist of four weekly deliveries within a fixed one-month cycle. Each product has an assigned delivery day, and customers may subscribe to multiple products simultaneously, with different products delivered on their respective scheduled days.

The owner initially proposed limiting these products to subscriptions, except for special high-volume purchases of approximately four dozen units or more. The subscription model is intended to support batch production and reduce operational expenses.

Customers may request to skip a delivery by notifying the bakery in advance. The skipped fulfillment is added to the end of the subscription cycle. Deliveries missed without advance notice are considered fulfilled.

Subscriptions are generally non-cancellable, although the owner is willing to consider exceptions involving illness, relocation, or other valid emergencies. If the bakery cannot fulfill a delivery because of severe weather or similar circumstances, customers will be notified and may receive compensation such as complimentary products.

The suggested subscription capacity is ten customers per product weekly. Should demand exceed production capability, the owners may consider hiring additional workers or purchasing equipment.

**Marketing and Social Media**

Kitchen406 does not maintain a regular social media posting schedule. The owner is responsible for preparing promotional content, while the co-owner also shares products through personal accounts.

At the time of the interview, the owner had created only two Facebook posts, one for Valentine's Day and another for Mother's Day. Posts primarily feature product advertisements and photographs and take only a few minutes to prepare. The Valentine's Day post appeared to generate more interest, although the owner could not determine whether the response resulted from the post itself or the occasion.

The bakery does not formally track sales generated by social media posts and generally responds to private messages rather than public comments. Current promotional content focuses on specific products, with possible expansion into seasonal campaigns.

The owner prefers promoting the bakery and its products without publicly emphasizing personal ownership. Reviewing posts individually or in batches would both be acceptable. Ideally, promotional content would be prepared approximately one week in advance, particularly for holidays, so production can be planned for resulting orders.

**Miscellaneous**

Future employees should have access only to order management and inventory-related functions rather than full administrative privileges.

The owner also expressed support for recording ingredient purchase quantities and prices during restocking, recognizing that this information would help the system generate useful product-cost and pricing analytics.

# 

# **1\. Introduction** {#1.-introduction}

## **1.1 Purpose** {#1.1-purpose}

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the detailed functional and non-functional requirements baseline for the development of Kitchen406: An Online Ordering and Product Management Platform with a Generative AI Marketing Assistant, Version 1.0. This document is the authoritative agreement between the developers and the client on what will be built. It is intended for the capstone panel, adviser, the development team, testers, and the two business owners.

## **1.2 Document Conventions** {#1.2-document-conventions}

Requirements are written using the form "The system shall..." to indicate mandatory behavior. The word "should" denotes a recommended but non-mandatory behavior, and "may" denotes an optional or permitted behavior. Each requirement is uniquely identified using module-based prefixes (e.g., FR-AUTH-01, FR-MKT-01) and is assigned a priority of High, Medium, or Low. High-priority requirements are essential to core system operation. Medium-priority requirements are important but not blocking. Low-priority requirements are desirable enhancements.

## **1.3 Intended Audience and Reading Suggestions** {#1.3-intended-audience-and-reading-suggestions}

This document is organized to first present overall product context (Section 2), followed by external interface requirements (Section 3), detailed system features and functional requirements (Section 4), and non-functional requirements (Section 5).

* Developers should read Sections 3-5 in full, as these sections define all technical requirements and integration specifications.  
* Testers should focus on Sections 4 and 5 to derive test cases and acceptance criteria.  
* Capstone panel, adviser, and the business owners may focus on Sections 1-2 for a high-level understanding of scope and product context, and Section 4 for feature-level detail.

## **1.4 Product Scope** {#1.4-product-scope}

Kitchen406 is a web-based platform designed specifically for the operations of Kitchen406, a home-based bakery. The system centralizes customer ordering, production planning, inventory monitoring, and business management within a single platform. Customers can browse products, place standard orders, enroll in prepaid subscriptions, submit custom cake requests, complete online payments, track orders and deliveries, and provide post-purchase feedback.

For the business, the platform supports product and recipe management, ingredient-based inventory tracking, production capacity control, cost-based pricing, order fulfillment, delivery coordination, customer feedback management, and sales analytics. Staff access is limited to the operational functions required for order fulfillment and inventory work, while administrative and sensitive business functions remain restricted to the owners. The system also includes an AI marketing assistant that automatically generates promotional caption-and-image drafts using current business information, with all generated content subject to owner review and approval before manual publication.

# **2\. Overall Description** {#2.-overall-description}

## **2.1 Product Perspective** {#2.1-product-perspective}

Kitchen406 is a new web-based platform developed specifically for the operations of Kitchen406, a home-based bakery in Metro Cebu. It centralizes processes currently handled through messages, spreadsheets, physical records, and manual monitoring into one system for customer transactions and bakery operations.

The platform consists of a customer-facing Web Storefront, an Owner-Admin Dashboard, and a restricted Staff Interface that use the same underlying product, order, inventory, and scheduling data. It also integrates with external services for QR Ph payments, location services, delivery, notifications, image storage, and AI-assisted marketing. The AI component is limited to generating marketing drafts for owner review and does not control ordering, payment, inventory, or fulfillment processes. The current design specifically separates customer, administrator, and staff access while keeping their information within the same platform.

## **2.2 Product Functions** {#2.2-product-functions}

The following summarizes the major functions the system will perform:

* Customer account and saved-address management.  
* Product catalog browsing and product availability.  
* Standard ordering through cart and checkout.  
* Prepaid four-week subscriptions with deferment support.  
* Custom cake requests, configuration, and quotations.  
* QR Ph online payment processing.  
* Order and delivery status tracking.  
* Bill of Materials-based inventory and material planning.  
* Production capacity control and scheduling.  
* Cost-based pricing and product margin calculation.  
* Sales and product analytics.  
* Customer ratings, reviews, and administrative moderation.  
* Email, SMS, and internal notifications.  
* Role-Based Access Control for owners and staff.  
* Event-triggered and weekly scheduled AI marketing draft generation with owner review.

## **2.3 User Classes and Characteristics** {#2.3-user-classes-and-characteristics}

| User Type | Technical Skill | Description | Key Capabilities |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Owner/Admin** | Basic to intermediate | Kitchen406 owners with full administrative access | Manage products, pricing, orders, subscriptions, custom cakes, inventory, capacity, deliveries, analytics, feedback, staff access, notifications, and AI marketing drafts. |
| **Staff** | Basic | Authorized bakery personnel responsible for operational tasks | View product and recipe information, process orders, update permitted order statuses, view schedules and delivery information, manage permitted inventory records, and receive operational notifications. |
| **Customer** | General public; browser literate | Registered customers using the Web Storefront | Browse products, manage addresses, place standard orders, enroll in subscriptions, request custom cakes, make payments, track orders and deliveries, receive notifications, and provide feedback. |
| **Guest** | General public; browser literate | Unregistered visitor | Browse publicly available products and information. Registration is required before completing transactions. |

## **2.4 Operating Environments** {#2.4-operating-environments}

* **Client side:** Web-based interface accessible through modern desktop and mobile browsers.  
* **Application:** Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Node.js.  
* **Database:** PostgreSQL with Prisma.  
* **Authentication:** Auth.js.  
* **Hosting:** Vercel for deployment and Railway for hosting PostgreSQL database and supporting background processes.  
* **External services:** Google Maps Platform, PayMongo, Lalamove, Brevo, Semaphore, Cloudinary, and Google Gemini API.  
* **Connectivity:** Internet connection required; no offline mode is specified.  
* **Market/currency**: Philippine market only, Philippine Peso (PHP) only.

## **2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints** {#2.5-design-and-implementation-constraints}

* The system shall be implemented as a web-based platform; no dedicated native mobile application is included.  
* All customer transactions shall require a registered account. Guest checkout is not supported.  
* Online payment shall use QR Ph through PayMongo, and payment must be confirmed before an order is finalized.  
* The system shall support three purchasing workflows: Standard Orders, Prepaid Subscriptions, and Custom Cake Requests.  
* Subscriptions shall follow a prepaid four-week delivery cycle and shall not use automatic recurring billing.  
* Production shall be controlled by configurable capacity limits, scheduling rules, and blocked dates.  
* Inventory and costing shall use recipe and Bill of Materials data linked to products and configurable custom-cake components. The current design distinguishes projected requirements, reservations, and actual inventory movements.  
* Access shall be controlled by user role. Owners have administrative access, while staff access is restricted to approved operational functions such as order fulfillment and inventory-related activities.  
* Delivery and location functions depend on Google Maps Platform and Lalamove for supported delivery workflows.  
* The AI marketing assistant shall be limited to generating promotional drafts from system data. Drafts remain subject to owner review and shall not be treated as automatic publication.  
* The system shall not require integration with specialized hardware such as POS terminals, barcode scanners, or kitchen display systems.  
* The accuracy of pricing, inventory, capacity, and other operational outputs depends on the data configured and maintained by the owners.

## **2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies** {#2.6-assumptions-and-dependencies}

* Users are assumed to have access to a stable internet connection and a modern web browser.  
* Customers are assumed to provide valid account, contact, address, and transaction information.  
* Owners and authorized staff are responsible for maintaining accurate product, recipe, ingredient-cost, inventory, capacity, and scheduling data.  
* The system depends on the availability and continued compatibility of PayMongo, Google Maps Platform, Lalamove, Brevo, Semaphore, Cloudinary, and Google Gemini API.  
* The owners are assumed to maintain the accounts, credentials, API access, credits, and subscriptions required by the third-party services used by the platform.  
* Payment confirmation depends on PayMongo successfully processing and reporting the QR Ph transaction.  
* Delivery quotation, booking, and tracking functions depend on Lalamove availability within the bakery's supported service area.  
* AI-generated promotional content depends on the availability of the configured generative AI service and on the accuracy of the operational data supplied to it.  
* System-generated inventory requirements, costing, and production schedules depend on correctly defined recipes, Bill of Materials records, stock information, and capacity settings.  
* The system assumes that owners will review generated marketing drafts before deciding whether to use them.

# **3\. External Interface Requirements** {#3.-external-interface-requirements}

## **3.1 User Interfaces** {#3.1-user-interfaces}

![][image39]

Figure 1\. Product Catalog

This interface displays the available Kitchen406 products in a browsable catalog, including product image, category, name, variant information, price, availability status, and subscription eligibility where applicable. Customers may filter products by category, search the catalog, and limit results to subscription-eligible products before opening a product detail page. While catalog data is loading, the interface shall display a loading state or placeholder product cards. If products cannot be retrieved, the page shall display an error message with an option to retry, while unavailable products shall remain visible but clearly marked as temporarily unavailable. 

![][image40]

Figure 2\. Product Details

This interface displays the selected product’s image, category, name, description, price, available variant, availability status, quantity controls, and Add to Cart action. Products eligible for subscription are identified separately and provide a link to the subscription plans while remaining available for standard purchase. While product data is loading, the page shall display a loading state and temporarily disable purchase controls. If the product cannot be loaded or an Add to Cart action fails, the interface shall display a clear error message and allow the user to retry. 

![][image41]

Figure 3\. Customer Reviews

This interface presents verified feedback from completed Kitchen406 orders, including the overall rating, rating distribution, individual customer ratings, purchased product, written comments, optional review images, and submission date. Unauthenticated users are prompted to sign in before submitting a review, while review eligibility is verified against completed purchases. While reviews are loading, the page shall display a loading state in place of the review content. If reviews cannot be retrieved, the interface shall display an error message with an option to retry without preventing access to the rest of the storefront. 

![][image42]

Figure 4\. Sign In Modal

This interface allows existing users to sign in using their registered email address and password, with controls for showing or hiding the password, recovering a forgotten password, and navigating to account registration. During authentication, the Sign In action shall indicate that the request is being processed and prevent repeated submissions. If the credentials are invalid or the sign-in request fails, the interface shall display a clear error message while preserving the entered email address and allowing the user to try again. 

![][image43]

Figure 5\. Sign Up Modal

This interface allows a new customer to create a Kitchen406 account by providing their first name, last name, email address, Philippine mobile number, password, and password confirmation. Password visibility controls are provided, and successful registration proceeds to email verification before the account becomes active. While registration is being processed, the Create Account action shall indicate a loading state and prevent duplicate submissions. Invalid, incomplete, duplicate, or failed registration attempts shall display clear field-level or form-level error messages while preserving valid entered information. 

![][image44]

Figure 6\. Email Verification Modal

This interface allows a newly registered customer to verify their email address by entering the six-digit verification code sent to the registered email. The interface displays the code expiration time and provides an option to request a new code when necessary. During verification or code resending, the corresponding action shall display a loading state and prevent repeated submissions. Invalid, expired, or failed verification attempts shall display an appropriate error message and allow the customer to retry or request another code. 

![][image45]

Figure 7\. Forgot Password Modal

This interface allows a user who cannot access their account to request password-reset instructions by entering their registered email address. After submission, the system sends the applicable reset instructions to the provided email and allows the user to return to the Sign In interface. While the request is being processed, the Send Reset Link action shall display a loading state and prevent duplicate requests. Invalid email input or failed reset requests shall display a clear error message, while the response should avoid unnecessarily revealing whether a particular email address is registered. 

![][image46]

Figure 8\. Cart

This interface displays the products currently added to the customer’s cart, including the selected variant, quantity, individual price, and controls for changing quantity or removing an item. An order summary shows the current subtotal and provides actions to continue shopping or proceed to checkout. While cart data or quantity changes are being processed, the affected controls shall display a loading state and prevent repeated actions. If the cart cannot be retrieved or updated, the interface shall display a clear error message and allow the customer to retry. 

![][image47]

Figure 9\. Checkout: Fulfillment

This interface allows the customer to choose between bakery pickup and courier delivery and select an available fulfillment date for the entire order. The calendar reflects scheduling restrictions such as passed dates, cut-off dates, unavailable batches, blocked dates, and available dates, while the order summary remains visible for reference. While fulfillment availability is being checked, the date-selection controls shall display a loading state and prevent continuation. If the selected date becomes unavailable or capacity cannot be verified, the system shall display an error and require the customer to choose another valid date. 

![][image48]

Figure 10\. Checkout: Delivery Address

This interface allows customers who selected courier delivery to choose a saved delivery address or add a new one. The selected location is shown on a map, together with its delivery-area status and the applicable delivery fee included in the order summary. While the address, route, or delivery quotation is being validated, the interface shall display a loading state and prevent continuation. If the address is outside the supported delivery area or location and delivery information cannot be retrieved, the system shall display an appropriate error and allow the customer to select or provide another address. 

![][image49]

Figure 11\. Checkout: Order Review

This interface presents the final order details before payment, including the selected products, fulfillment method and date, delivery address where applicable, QR Ph payment method, delivery fee, and total amount due. Customers may return to edit the cart, fulfillment details, or delivery address before proceeding to payment. While final availability, capacity, inventory, or pricing information is being verified, the payment action shall remain disabled. If any required information has changed or can no longer be validated, the interface shall display an error and direct the customer to correct the affected checkout information. 

![][image50]

Figure 12\. Payment

This interface displays the QR Ph payment session, including the amount due, QR code, session expiration time, order summary, and fulfillment information. The customer scans the QR code using a supported banking or e-wallet application while the system waits for payment confirmation. While the payment session is being created or payment status is being verified, the interface shall show a processing state. If the QR session expires or payment fails, the interface shall display the applicable status and provide a way to retry payment without confirming the order. 

![][image51]

Figure 13\. Order Confirmation

This interface confirms that payment has been successfully completed and that the order has entered the fulfillment process. It displays the order reference, confirmation status, order summary, fulfillment information, payment details, and navigation options for viewing the order, opening the customer’s orders, or continuing shopping. While confirmation details are being loaded after payment, the interface shall display a loading state without initiating another payment. If the confirmation page cannot be retrieved, the system shall allow the customer to retry loading the stored order information. 

![][image52]

Figure 14\. Customer Orders List

This interface displays the customer’s previous and current orders with their reference numbers, products, fulfillment information, totals, and current statuses. Customers may filter orders by status, search by order reference or product, select an order type, change the sorting order, and open an individual order for more details. While order records are loading, the page shall display a loading state or placeholder entries. If no matching orders exist, an empty-results state shall be shown, while retrieval errors shall display a retry option. 

![][image53]

Figure 15\. Customer Order Details

This interface provides detailed information for a selected order, including its reference, current status, progress through fulfillment, activity history, fulfillment information, payment details, and order summary. It also provides supporting actions such as copying the order reference, contacting the bakery, and viewing related order information. While the order record is loading, the interface shall display a loading state. If the order details cannot be retrieved, the system shall display an error message and allow the customer to retry without altering the order itself. 

![][image54]

Figure 16\. Subscription Eligible Products

This interface displays products that may be enrolled in Kitchen406’s four-week subscription program, grouped by applicable product categories. Each product card shows its subscription availability, variant information, per-delivery price, four-delivery subtotal, and actions for setting up a subscription or purchasing the product as a standard order. Subscription availability and standard-order availability are presented separately so that a product may remain purchasable normally even when its subscription slots are unavailable. While subscription availability is loading, product actions shall remain disabled or show a loading state, and retrieval errors shall provide a clear retry option. 

![][image55]

Figure 17\. Subscription Configuration

This interface allows the customer to configure a four-week subscription by selecting the product variant, quantity per delivery, and an available weekly subscription schedule. The interface previews all four scheduled fulfillments and provides a running summary showing the selected product, schedule, fulfillment method, first and final delivery dates, and product subtotal. While available schedules or subscription capacity are being checked, the affected controls shall display a loading state and continuation shall be disabled. If the selected configuration is no longer available, the interface shall display an error and require another valid configuration before proceeding. 

![][image56]

Figure 18\. Subscription Review

This interface allows the customer to review the complete subscription before payment, including the chosen product configuration, four scheduled fulfillment dates, delivery address where applicable, subscription schedule, delivery charges, and full prepaid total. Customers may return to edit the subscription configuration or delivery address before continuing to payment. While the system performs final schedule, capacity, delivery, and pricing checks, the payment action shall remain disabled. If any scheduled fulfillment can no longer be accommodated, the system shall display an error and require the affected subscription details to be revised. 

![][image57]

Figure 19\. Customer Subscriptions List

This interface displays the customer’s subscription records, including their status, subscribed product, variant, amount paid, delivery progress, and next scheduled fulfillment. Customers may filter between active and completed subscriptions, search by reference or product, sort the results, explore additional subscription offerings, and open an individual subscription for details. While subscription records are being retrieved, the page shall display a loading state or placeholders. If no subscriptions match the current filter, an empty state shall be shown, while retrieval failures shall provide an option to retry. 

![][image58]

Figure 20\. Subscription Details

This interface presents the complete information for an active subscription, including its product and variant, current status, completed-delivery progress, next scheduled fulfillment, full four-week schedule, pickup or delivery information, and prepaid pricing details. Each weekly fulfillment may be opened individually, and an eligible upcoming delivery provides access to the deferment process. While subscription or fulfillment information is loading, the interface shall show a loading state. If a deferment is no longer available or the required subscription information cannot be retrieved, the affected action shall be disabled and an appropriate error message shall be displayed. 

![][image59]

Figure 21\. Defer Subscription Delivery

This interface allows an eligible customer to request rescheduling of one upcoming subscription fulfillment while leaving the remaining scheduled deliveries unchanged. It displays the current delivery, available replacement schedule options, the updated four-delivery preview, and the remaining deferment allowance before the customer confirms the request. While replacement dates and production capacity are being checked, the confirmation action shall remain disabled and a loading state shall be shown. If neither date has capacity, the interface indicates that deferment is unavailable. When the customer confirms an available date, the system applies the deferment. If the request is ineligible, the system retains the original schedule and allowance.

![][image60]

Figure 22\. Custom Cake Introduction

This interface introduces the custom cake service and explains the process of choosing cake options, submitting reference images, receiving a quotation, and completing payment. Customers may begin a new request or open their existing cake requests. The interface clarifies that the bakery reviews each request before providing a final quotation. If authentication is required when starting a request, the system shall direct the customer to sign in before continuing.

![][image61]  
Figure 23\. Custom Cake Request

This interface allows customers to begin a custom cake request by selecting a requested date and saved delivery address. Customers may add or edit an address and review their contact information before continuing, while a summary displays the current selections and preliminary estimate. The calendar reflects lead time, cutoff, blocked dates, and custom cake capacity, and the interface informs customers that their requested date remains subject to availability until payment is completed and the order is confirmed. While availability is being checked, continuation shall remain disabled. Invalid fulfillment details or failed checks shall display a clear message and allow the customer to revise the request.

![][image62]

Figure 24\. Cake Options / Add-ons

This interface allows customers to configure their cake by selecting its shape, flavor, size, color, and icing. Each option displays its name, description, price contribution, and availability, while the request summary shows the selected configuration, any included add-on charges, and preliminary estimate. Unavailable options remain visible but cannot be selected. While cake options are loading, the interface shall display a loading state and prevent continuation. If options cannot be retrieved, an error message and retry action shall appear, while incomplete configurations shall require the customer to complete the necessary selections.

![][image63]

Figure 25\. Reference Image & Notes

This interface allows customers to provide one required primary reference image and up to two optional additional images for their cake design. Customers may preview, enlarge, replace, or remove images and enter optional design notes using a text field with a character counter. Supported image formats and file-size limits are displayed beside the upload controls. While an image is being checked, the interface shall indicate its processing status. Unsupported, oversized, or unreadable images shall display clear errors, and continuation shall remain disabled until the required reference image has been successfully validated.

![][image64]

Figure 26\. Custom Cake Request Summary

This interface presents the complete cake request before submission, including the configuration, any selected add-ons, reference images, design notes, requested schedule, delivery address, contact information, and preliminary estimate. Customers may return to earlier steps to revise their selections. The interface explains that the owner will review the request and issue a final quotation, with no payment collected during submission. While submission is being processed, the submission action shall display a loading state and prevent duplicate requests. Changed estimates shall require acceptance, while validation or submission failures shall preserve the draft and display a clear error.

![][image65]

Figure 27\. Quotation Details / Acceptance

This interface displays the cake quotation, including its version, status, specifications, reference images, customer notes, bakery review, agreed fulfillment details, expiration, and itemized total. Customers may view earlier quotation versions, accept an eligible quotation through confirmation, or decline it with optional notes. Acceptance proceeds to full QR Ph payment before order confirmation. While acceptance is being processed, repeated submissions shall be prevented. Expired, superseded, or unavailable quotations shall display an explanatory message, while pending verification or recorded-payment notices shall direct customers to the appropriate record without encouraging another payment.

![][image66]

Figure 28\. Customer Cake Requests List

## **3.2 Hardware Interfaces** {#3.2-hardware-interfaces}

The system does not integrate with any hardware peripherals. No POS terminals, kitchen display systems, barcode scanners, or printers are required or supported. All interactions occur through a standard web browser on any internet-connected device.

## **3.3 Software Interfaces** {#3.3-software-interfaces}

| Interface | Purpose | Data Exchanged |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **PostgreSQL Database** | Store the platform's accounts, products, orders, subscriptions, custom cake requests, inventory, recipes, payments, notifications, feedback, and other system records. | Application data through Prisma database operations |
| **Google Maps Platform** | Support address search, map display, location validation, and route/distance calculations. | Address queries, place information, coordinates, route and distance data |
| **PayMongo API v2** | Process QR Ph payments and obtain payment status information. | Payment amount, transaction reference, QR Ph payment information, and payment status |
| **Lalamove API v3** | Obtain delivery quotations, create supported delivery bookings, and receive delivery status information. | Pickup/drop-off locations, delivery details, quotation data, booking information, and delivery status |
| **Semaphore API v2.16** | Send SMS notifications to customers. | Recipient mobile number and notification message |
| **Brevo API** | Send email notifications generated by the system. | Recipient email address, subject, and notification content |
| **Cloudinary** | Store and retrieve images used by the platform. | Product images, uploaded images, generated image files, and image URLs |
| **Google Gemini API** | Generate data-grounded promotional drafts for the AI Marketing Assistant. | Relevant system context, generation requests, generated captions, and image output |
| **Auth.js** | Provide authentication and session management for system users. | Authentication credentials, account/session information, and user role information |

## **3.4 Communications Interfaces** {#3.4-communications-interfaces}

* **EIR-COM-01:** All communication between the client application and the server shall occur through secure HTTPS connections.  
* **EIR-COM-02:** Communication between the Kitchen406 server and supported third-party APIs shall use HTTPS-based API requests.  
* **EIR-COM-03:** The system shall receive and process payment-status updates from PayMongo for QR Ph transactions.  
* **EIR-COM-04:** The system shall communicate with Lalamove to request delivery quotations, submit supported delivery bookings, and receive available delivery-status updates.  
* **EIR-COM-05:** The system shall communicate with Google Maps Platform to retrieve address, location, route, and distance information.  
* **EIR-COM-06:** The system shall send customer SMS notifications through the Semaphore API.  
* **EIR-COM-07:** The system shall send email notifications through the Brevo API.  
* **EIR-COM-08:** The system shall communicate with Cloudinary for the upload and retrieval of platform images.  
* **EIR-COM-09:** The system shall communicate with the Google Gemini API when generating promotional content for the AI Marketing Assistant.  
* **EIR-COM-10:** Third-party service credentials and API keys shall be handled on the server side and shall not be exposed through the customer-facing client application.

# **4\. System Features** {#4.-system-features}

## **4.1 Authentication and Access Control** {#4.1-authentication-and-access-control}

### **4.1.1 Description and Priority** {#4.1.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages registration, authentication, account verification, password recovery, sessions, and role-based access for customers, staff, and administrators. **Priority: High.**

### **4.1.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.1.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a new customer submits valid registration information, the system creates a customer account and associates it with a customer profile.  
* When a registered user submits valid login credentials, the system authenticates the account and provides access according to the user's assigned role.  
* When a user submits invalid login credentials, the system rejects the authentication attempt and displays an appropriate error message.  
* When a user requests password recovery, the system initiates the account-verification process before allowing the password to be changed.  
* When an authenticated staff user attempts to access an administrator-only function, the system denies access according to the configured role permissions.  
* When an authenticated user logs out, the system terminates the active session.

### **4.1.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.1.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-AUTH-01 | The system shall allow customers to create a registered account. | High |
| FR-AUTH-02 | The system shall require authentication before a customer can complete a transaction. | High |
| FR-AUTH-03 | The system shall authenticate registered users using their account credentials. | High |
| FR-AUTH-04 | The system shall support customer, staff, and administrator access roles. | High |
| FR-AUTH-05 | The system shall restrict functions according to the authenticated user's role. | High |
| FR-AUTH-06 | The system shall provide an account-verification and password-recovery process. | High |
| FR-AUTH-07 | The system shall prevent staff users from accessing functions reserved for administrators. | High |

## **4.2 Customer Profile Management** {#4.2-customer-profile-management}

### **4.2.1 Description and Priority** {#4.2.1-description-and-priority}

This feature allows registered customers to maintain their personal account information and view records associated with their account. **Priority: Medium.**

### **4.2.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.2.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer opens their profile, the system displays the personal information associated with the authenticated customer account.  
* When a customer updates permitted profile information, the system validates the submitted information and saves the changes.  
* When a customer enters invalid profile information, the system rejects the changes and identifies the fields that require correction.  
* When a customer opens their transaction history, the system displays the orders and other transactions associated with the customer profile.  
* When another user attempts to access a customer's private profile information without authorization, the system denies the request.

### **4.2.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.2.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-PROF-01 | The system shall allow customers to view their profile information. | Medium |
| FR-PROF-02 | The system shall allow customers to update permitted profile information. | Medium |
| FR-PROF-03 | The system shall associate the customer's orders, subscriptions, custom cake requests, addresses, and feedback with their customer profile. | High |
| FR-PROF-04 | The system shall allow customers to view their transaction history. | Medium |

## **4.3 Staff Account Management** {#4.3-staff-account-management}

### **4.3.1 Description and Priority** {#4.3.1-description-and-priority}

This feature allows administrators to manage staff accounts and control staff access to operational functions. **Priority: High.**

### **4.3.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.3.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an administrator submits valid information for a new staff member, the system creates the staff account and associates it with the administrator who created it.  
* When an administrator modifies an existing staff account, the system validates and saves the updated account information.  
* When an administrator deactivates a staff account, the system prevents that account from accessing the staff interface.  
* When an active staff member logs in, the system grants access only to the operational functions permitted for the staff role.  
* When a staff member attempts to access owner-only functions, the system denies access.

### **4.3.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.3.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-STAFF-01 | The system shall allow administrators to create staff accounts. | High |
| FR-STAFF-02 | The system shall allow administrators to update or deactivate staff accounts. | High |
| FR-STAFF-03 | The system shall associate each staff account with the administrator who created it. | Medium |
| FR-STAFF-04 | The system shall restrict staff access to authorized operational functions. | High |
| FR-STAFF-05 | The system shall prevent staff from accessing owner-only financial, analytics, pricing, customer-management, and AI marketing functions. | High |

## **4.4 Delivery Address Management** {#4.4-delivery-address-management}

### **4.4.1 Description and Priority** {#4.4.1-description-and-priority}

This feature allows customers to save and reuse delivery addresses and supports address validation through Google Maps Platform. **Priority: High.**

### **4.4.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.4.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer enters a delivery address, the system provides address-search and location-validation support through Google Maps Platform.  
* When a customer saves a valid delivery address, the system stores it under the authenticated customer's profile.  
* When a customer adds more than one delivery address, the system maintains each address as a separate saved record.  
* When a customer designates a saved address as the default, the system updates the default-address selection for that customer.  
* When a customer selects a saved address during an applicable transaction, the system loads the stored delivery information for use in checkout.  
* When a customer edits or removes a saved address, the system updates the customer's address records accordingly.

* When an administrator updates an existing product or variant, the system saves the changes and reflects them in the storefront.  
* When an administrator deactivates a product, the system prevents the product from being selected for new customer transactions.

## **4.6 Shopping Cart Management** {#4.6-shopping-cart-management}

### **4.6.1 Description and Priority** {#4.6.1-description-and-priority}

This feature allows customers to collect standard catalog products and quantities before proceeding to checkout. **Priority: High.**

### **4.6.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.6.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer adds an available product to the cart, the system stores the selected product variant and quantity in the customer's cart.  
* When a customer increases or decreases an item's quantity, the system updates the quantity and recalculates the cart subtotal.  
* When a customer removes an item from the cart, the system removes the selected item and recalculates the cart subtotal.  
* When a customer opens the cart, the system displays the selected products, quantities, prices, and current subtotal.  
* When a customer attempts to proceed with an unavailable item or invalid quantity, the system prevents checkout until the cart is corrected.  
* When a customer selects Proceed to Checkout, the system forwards the valid cart contents to the checkout process.

* When an authorized user updates an order's status, the system records the new status and preserves the status change in the order history.  
* When a customer opens an existing standard order, the system displays the current order information and status available to that customer.  
* When payment for a pending standard transaction is unsuccessful, the system does not confirm the order.

## **4.8 Subscription Management** {#4.8-subscription-management}

### **4.8.1 Description and Priority** {#4.8.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages Kitchen406's prepaid subscription workflow consisting of four scheduled deliveries. **Priority: High.**

### **4.8.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.8.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer selects an eligible subscription offering, the system displays the applicable subscription schedule and transaction information.  
* When a customer selects a subscription schedule, the system checks the required production capacity before the subscription commitment is finalized.

* When the customer successfully completes the payment, the system creates four scheduled delivery records, confirms their capacity allocations, and retains the first fulfillment's ingredient reservation. Ingredient requirements for later fulfillments remain projected until their respective reservation dates.

* When a subscription delivery is completed, the system updates the delivery record and the subscription's remaining fulfillments.  
* When a customer submits a deferment request before the affected fulfillment’s preparation day begins, the system checks capacity for the next-day date and the date one week after the subscription’s final scheduled fulfillment. It offers only dates with sufficient capacity. If the customer confirms one offered date and the deferment allowance is unused, the system automatically reschedules the affected fulfillment and records the replacement allocation. If neither date has sufficient capacity, the system rejects the request and retains the original schedule and allowance.  
* When a subscription delivery is deferred, the system preserves the original delivery and capacity information rather than overwriting the previous record.  
* When a customer views an active subscription, the system displays its delivery schedule, completed deliveries, remaining deliveries, and applicable status information.

### **4.8.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.8.3-functional-requirements}

| ----- | ----- | ----- |

| FR-SUB-02 | The system shall require full prepaid payment for the four-week subscription. | High |
| FR-SUB-03 | The system shall create four scheduled subscription delivery records for each successful subscription. | High |
| FR-SUB-04 | The system shall track the remaining and completed subscription deliveries. | High |
| FR-SUB-05 | The system shall allow customers to request deferment of an upcoming, unfulfilled subscription delivery. | High |
| FR-SUB-06 | A deferred delivery shall be rescheduled without reducing the customer's total number of deliveries. | High |
| FR-SUB-07 | The system shall maintain the original and replacement capacity allocations associated with a deferment. | High |
| FR-SUB-08 | The system shall limit each subscription to one confirmed deferment. Rejected or ineligible requests shall not consume the allowance. | High |
| FR-SUB-09 | The system shall automatically apply a deferment after the customer confirms an offered replacement date with sufficient capacity, provided the request is timely and the deferment allowance is unused. Manual Admin/Owner approval is not required. | High |
| FR-SUB-10 | The system shall retain the original delivery schedule and deferment allowance when a request is rejected or cannot be accommodated. | High |
| FR-SUB-11 | The system shall accept deferment requests only before the configured preparation day of the affected fulfillment begins. | High |
| FR-SUB-12 | The system shall check only two deferment replacement dates: the next day and one week after the subscription’s final scheduled fulfillment. It shall offer a date only when that date has sufficient production capacity and shall not search for a later replacement date. | High |

* When a customer accepts a quotation, the system records the selected quotation as the accepted quotation for the request.

## **4.10 Checkout and Payment Management** {#4.10-checkout-and-payment-management}

### **4.10.1 Description and Priority** {#4.10.1-description-and-priority}

This feature validates a transaction before submission and processes full online payment through PayMongo QR Ph. **Priority: High.**

### **4.10.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.10.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer proceeds to checkout, the system verifies that the customer is authenticated before allowing the transaction to continue.  
* When a customer reviews the checkout page, the system displays the selected items, applicable prices, fulfillment information, and transaction total.  
* When a customer selects a fulfillment schedule, the system validates the applicable inventory, capacity, blocked-date, cut-off, and scheduling requirements before payment.  
* When a customer selects delivery, the system validates the selected delivery address and obtains the applicable delivery quotation for the supported workflow.  
* When all checkout requirements are satisfied, the system calculates the final amount payable and allows the customer to proceed to QR Ph payment.  
* When payment begins, the system creates a 30-minute PayMongo QR Ph session and a 32-minute checkout hold.  
* When full payment is verified before hold expiration, the system confirms the order and retains its reservations.  
* When payment remains unconfirmed at hold expiration, the system checks its status with PayMongo.  
* When payment fails, expires, or remains unresolved after verification, the system cancels the order and releases reservations.  
* When payment is verified after reservation release, the system retains the cancelled order and records the payment as eligible for an external refund.  
* When payment status changes, the system updates the associated transaction record for confirmation or reconciliation.

### **4.10.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.10.3-functional-requirements}

| ----- | ----- | ----- |

| FR-PAY-02 | The system shall validate applicable product, inventory, scheduling, and capacity requirements before payment. | High |
| FR-PAY-03 | The system shall calculate the total amount payable before payment begins. | High |
| FR-PAY-04 | The system shall use PayMongo QR Ph for online payment processing. | High |
| FR-PAY-05 | The system shall require verified full payment through PayMongo before confirming an order. | High |
| FR-PAY-06 | The system shall record payment statuses and verify unresolved transactions with PayMongo when the checkout hold expires. | High |

| FR-PAY-08 | The system shall maintain a 30-minute QR Ph payment session and a 32-minute checkout hold, including a two-minute allowance for payment confirmation. | High |

## **4.11 Production Capacity and Scheduling** {#4.11-production-capacity-and-scheduling}

### **4.11.1 Description and Priority** {#4.11.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages the bakery’s configurable production limits and scheduling constraints for standard orders, subscriptions, and custom cakes. It prevents overbooking by validating requested fulfillment dates against the applicable capacity limits, blocked dates, cut-off times, and lead-time requirements before an order commitment is accepted. Production capacity is maintained separately for each purchasing workflow and may be adjusted by the Admin/Owner according to the bakery’s current operational capability. **Priority: High.**

### **4.11.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.11.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer selects a fulfillment date during checkout, the system checks the date against the applicable production capacity, blocked dates, cut-off rules, and required lead time.  
* When a customer selects a date whose applicable capacity has already been reached, the system prevents the customer from proceeding with that date and requires another valid fulfillment date.  
* When customer selects a date that has been blocked by the Admin/Owner, the system prevents new bookings for that date.  
* When a customer begins checkout for an available fulfillment date, the system temporarily holds the required production capacity while the payment transaction is in progress.  
* When the customer successfully completes payment, the system converts the temporary capacity hold into a confirmed capacity allocation for the order.  
* When the checkout or payment transaction does not proceed, the system releases the temporarily held production capacity so that it becomes available for other transactions.  
* When an Admin/Owner modifies a capacity limit or scheduling restriction, the system applies the updated configuration when validating subsequent bookings.  
* When a subscription delivery or confirmed deferment requires a scheduled fulfillment date, the system validates the corresponding subscription capacity before allocating the delivery.

### **4.11.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.11.3-functional-requirements}

| FR-CAP-03 | The system shall evaluate production capacity according to the requested fulfillment date rather than the date on which the transaction is placed. | High |

## **4.12 Inventory Management** {#4.12-inventory-management}

### **4.12.1 Description and Priority** {#4.12.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages Kitchen406’s ingredient stock and the inventory movements associated with restocking, order requirements, consumption, and manual adjustments. The system uses recipe and Bill of Materials information maintained elsewhere in the platform to determine the ingredients required by orders, project material consumption, reserve stock during checkout, update inventory as stock is consumed or replenished, and identify shortages that may affect product availability. Both the Admin/Owner and authorized Staff can perform routine inventory operations. **Priority: High.**

### **4.12.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.12.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an Admin/Owner or Staff member opens the inventory records, the system displays the current recorded stock quantities of the bakery’s ingredients.  
* When a confirmed order requires ingredients, the system determines the required quantities using the applicable recipe or Bill of Materials and reflects the expected ingredient consumption in inventory planning.  
* When a customer enters checkout, the system temporarily reserves the ingredients required for standard orders, custom cakes, or the first subscription fulfillment.  
* When the customer successfully completes payment, the system retains the required stock allocation for the confirmed order.  
* One day before a subsequent subscription fulfillment's scheduled preparation date, the system attempts to reserve its required ingredients.  
* If insufficient stock prevents reservation, the system notifies the Admin/Owner and allows the reservation to be retried after restocking.  
* When the checkout or payment transaction expires or fails to proceed, the system releases the temporarily reserved ingredient quantities.  
* When an ingredient reaches its configured low-stock threshold, the system alerts the Admin/Owner that replenishment is required.  
* When a required ingredient becomes fully depleted, the system prevents affected products from being ordered while the required ingredient remains unavailable.  
* When an Admin/Owner or Staff member records newly purchased ingredients, the system increases the corresponding recorded stock and records the restocking movement.  
* When an Admin/Owner or Staff member finds a discrepancy between physical and recorded stock, the user records an inventory adjustment and the system updates the stock quantity while preserving the reason for the adjustment.  
* When ingredient stock is consumed, replenished, reversed, or adjusted, the system records the resulting inventory movement for traceability.

### **4.12.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.12.3-functional-requirements}

## **4.13 Recipe and Bill of Materials Management** {#4.13-recipe-and-bill-of-materials-management}

### **4.13.1 Description and Priority** {#4.13.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages the recipe and Bill of Materials (BoM) definitions used to connect sellable products and configurable cake components to the raw ingredients required for production. The Admin/Owner maintains the ingredient requirements and quantities associated with product variations, while authorized Staff may view recipe details for production purposes without being permitted to modify the underlying recipes. Kitchen406 uses a single-level BoM structure in which finished products are linked directly to base ingredients rather than to separately tracked intermediate or prepared components. **Priority: High.**

### **4.13.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.13.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an Admin/Owner opens the recipe information for a product variation, the system displays the ingredients and quantities currently associated with that variation.  
* When an Admin/Owner modifies the ingredient composition or required quantity of a product variation, the system updates the corresponding BoM definition.  
* When an Admin/Owner associates an ingredient with a configurable custom-cake option or add-on, the system stores the ingredient requirement so that the selected configuration can be included in material calculations.  
* When a confirmed or pending order requires a product variation, the system reads the associated BoM to determine the raw ingredients and quantities required for that order.  
* When a custom cake includes configured options or add-ons, the system uses the corresponding ingredient mappings to determine their required materials.  
* When a Staff member views a recipe during production, the system displays the required ingredients and quantities but does not allow the Staff member to alter the recipe.  
* When a recipe is used for costing, the system makes the defined ingredient quantities and associated inventory cost data available to the pricing calculation.

### **4.13.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.13.3-functional-requirements}

| FR-BOM-02 | The system shall allow a product variation to be associated with multiple required ingredients. | High |
| FR-BOM-03 | The system shall store the required quantity of each ingredient associated with a product variation. | High |
| FR-BOM-04 | The system shall allow the same ingredient to be referenced by the recipes of multiple product variations. | High |
| FR-BOM-05 | The system shall associate recipe ingredient records with the corresponding inventory items used for stock and costing calculations. | High |

| FR-BOM-07 | The system shall use the defined recipe or BoM to determine the ingredient quantities required when an applicable product is included in an order. | High |

| FR-BOM-09 | The system shall make recipe-defined ingredient quantities and their associated costs available to the pricing and costing feature. | High |
| FR-BOM-10 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner and authorized Staff to view recipe details required for production. | High |
