## **4.14 Pricing and Costing Management** {#4.14-pricing-and-costing-management}

### **4.14.1 Description and Priority** {#4.14.1-description-and-priority}

This feature provides the Admin/Owner with cost-based pricing support derived from the bakery's own recipe and inventory data. The system calculates each product's estimated production cost from its ingredient and packaging costs together with a configurable utility-overhead value, applies the configured markup percentage to produce a suggested selling price, and displays the resulting estimated production cost and profit-margin information for owner review. The suggested price serves only as decision support and does not automatically replace the product's final selling price. **Priority: High.**

### **4.14.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.14.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an Admin/Owner views the costing information for a product variation, the system calculates and displays its current production cost and suggested selling price.  
* When the cost of an ingredient used by a product changes, the system uses the updated cost data when calculating that product's production cost and suggested price.  
* When an Admin/Owner changes the general utility-overhead value, the system uses the updated value in subsequent pricing calculations for products that do not have an individual override.  
* When an Admin/Owner configures a product-specific utility-overhead value, the system uses the override instead of the general default when costing that product.  
* When an Admin/Owner changes the markup percentage, the system recalculates suggested prices using the updated markup.  
* When the system produces a suggested selling price, the Admin/Owner reviews the recommendation and decides whether to retain or change the product's final selling price.  
* When an Admin/Owner changes a final selling price, the system stores the selected selling price separately from the system-generated suggested price.

### **4.14.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.14.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-PRICE-01 | The system shall restrict pricing and costing configuration to the Admin/Owner. | High |
| FR-PRICE-02 | The system shall calculate the material cost of a product using the ingredient quantities defined in its recipe or BoM and the corresponding recorded ingredient costs. | High |
| FR-PRICE-03 | The system shall include applicable packaging cost as a direct material cost when determining the product's production cost. | High |
| FR-PRICE-04 | The system shall include a utility-overhead value representing applicable gas and electricity costs in the product's production-cost calculation. | High |
| FR-PRICE-05 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to configure a general default utility-overhead value. | High |
| FR-PRICE-06 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to configure a product-specific utility-overhead override when the product's production requirements differ from the general default. | High |
| FR-PRICE-07 | The system shall use the product-specific utility-overhead value when one exists. Otherwise, it shall use the configured general utility-overhead value. | High |
| FR-PRICE-08 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to configure the markup percentage used for suggested-price calculations. | High |
| FR-PRICE-09 | The system shall calculate a suggested selling price using the computed production cost and configured markup percentage. | High |
| FR-PRICE-10 | The system shall display the estimated production cost, suggested selling price, and estimated profit margin to the Admin/Owner. | High |
| FR-PRICE-11 | The system shall maintain the suggested selling price separately from the final selling price selected by the Admin/Owner. | High |
| FR-PRICE-12 | The system shall not automatically replace a product's final selling price with the calculated suggested price. | High |
| FR-PRICE-13 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to determine and save the final selling price after reviewing the system's pricing information. | High |
| FR-PRICE-14 | The system shall use updated ingredient cost, recipe, utility-overhead, and markup information in subsequent pricing calculations. | High |
| FR-PRICE-15 | The system shall make product cost and margin information available for use in the Admin/Owner's reports and analytics views. | Medium |
| FR-PRICE-16 | The system shall calculate the estimated profit margin as ((selling price − production cost) / selling price) × 100, excluding delivery, marketing, and other costs outside the estimated production cost. | Medium |

## **4.15 Order Fulfillment Management** {#4.15-order-fulfillment-management}

### **4.15.1 Description and Priority** {#4.15.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages confirmed orders from the point at which they enter production until they are ready for their selected fulfillment method. Authorized Staff can view active and upcoming orders, access the product or custom-cake information required for preparation, consult the production schedule, and update order statuses as fulfillment progresses. The Admin/Owner can monitor all confirmed orders and their overall fulfillment progress, while registered customers can view the current status and fulfillment details of their own transactions. Delivery-provider operations themselves are handled separately under Delivery Management. **Priority: High.**

### **4.15.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.15.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer's payment is successfully confirmed, the system places the corresponding order into the confirmed-order workflow for production and fulfillment.  
* When a Staff member opens the active-order view, the system displays confirmed orders requiring preparation and their relevant fulfillment information.  
* When a Staff member checks the production schedule, the system displays the orders and fulfillments associated with upcoming scheduled dates.  
* When a Staff member opens an order, the system displays the product, quantity, fulfillment, and applicable preparation information required to complete the order.  
* When a Staff member opens a custom-cake order, the system displays the approved custom-cake details needed for preparation.  
* When preparation of an order progresses, an authorized Staff member updates its status and the system records the new fulfillment state.  
* When an order becomes ready, the system reflects the updated order status so that the customer and Admin/Owner can see that progress.  
* When an Admin/Owner opens order management, the system displays confirmed orders and their fulfillment progress.  
* When a registered customer views an order, the system displays the current order status together with the selected fulfillment date and fulfillment method.  
* When an order requiring delivery reaches the appropriate fulfillment stage, the order becomes available for the separate delivery-management process.

### **4.15.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.15.3-functional-requirements}

| FR-FUL-03 | The system shall allow authorized Staff to view upcoming fulfillment requirements through the production schedule. | High |
| FR-FUL-04 | The system shall display the selected fulfillment date and fulfillment method associated with each confirmed order. | High |

| FR-FUL-06 | The system shall provide authorized Staff with the approved custom-cake details required to prepare confirmed custom-cake orders. | High |
| FR-FUL-07 | The system shall allow authorized Staff to access applicable recipe information required during order preparation. | High |
| FR-FUL-08 | The system shall allow authorized Staff to update the status of an order as it progresses through production and fulfillment. | High |
| FR-FUL-09 | The system shall reflect whether an order is still being prepared, is ready, or has progressed further through the applicable fulfillment process. | High |
| FR-FUL-10 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to view all confirmed orders and monitor their fulfillment progress. | High |
| FR-FUL-11 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to view both current and upcoming confirmed transactions. | High |

## **4.16 Delivery Management** {#4.16-delivery-management}

### **4.16.1 Description and Priority** {#4.16.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages the delivery-related processes for standard orders and subscription fulfillments, including service-area verification, delivery-fee quotation, courier booking, and delivery-status tracking. Google Maps Platform is used to validate the selected delivery location and determine whether it falls within the bakery's serviceable area, while Lalamove provides delivery quotations, booking, and subsequent status updates. Courier booking is performed by the Admin/Owner only after an order is ready for delivery. Custom cake delivery is excluded from this feature because it is handled manually by the owners outside the system. **Priority: High.**

### **4.16.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.16.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer selects delivery as the fulfillment method, the system uses the selected delivery address for location and delivery processing.  
* When a delivery address is selected during checkout, the system validates the location and determines whether it falls within Kitchen406's serviceable area.  
* When the delivery address is outside the serviceable area, the system prevents the customer from proceeding with delivery to that address.  
* When a customer proceeds with an eligible delivery order, the system requests a delivery quotation from Lalamove and includes the returned delivery fee in the order summary.  
* When payment for a delivery order is completed, the system stores the required delivery information with the confirmed order without immediately booking a courier.  
* When an applicable standard order or subscription fulfillment becomes ready for delivery, the Admin/Owner initiates the Lalamove booking using the delivery information already associated with the order.  
* When Lalamove reports a delivery-status change, the system updates the corresponding delivery status.  
* When a  customer views an order with an active Lalamove delivery, the system displays the latest delivery status received from Lalamove.  
* When a custom cake becomes ready for delivery, no courier booking is performed by the system because custom cake delivery is handled independently by the owners.

## **4.17 Notification Management** {#4.17-notification-management}

### **4.17.1 Description and Priority** {#4.17.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages automated customer and internal system notifications generated by relevant events within Kitchen406. Customer communications are delivered through Brevo for email and Semaphore for SMS, while internal system notifications may be presented to authorized administrative or staff users. The system also maintains records of outgoing notifications, their associated activity, provider, and sending status to reduce the need for repetitive manual customer messaging. **Priority: High.**

### **4.17.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.17.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an order is successfully confirmed, the system sends the applicable order-confirmation notification to the customer.  
* When an order status changes at a notification-relevant stage, the system sends the applicable update to the customer.  
* When Lalamove reports a delivery-status change, the system sends the applicable delivery update to the customer.  
* When a scheduled subscription delivery is approaching, the system sends the applicable subscription reminder to the customer.  
* When an order or schedule change affects Staff operations, the system creates an internal system notification for the applicable staff users.  
* When an external notification is sent, the system records the notification type, provider, sending status, recipient context, and associated system activity.  
* When delivery of an external notification encounters an issue, the system retains the applicable sending and retry information in the notification record.

## **4.18 Customer Review Management** {#4.18-customer-review-management}

### **4.18.1 Description and Priority** {#4.18.1-description-and-priority}

This feature allows registered customers to submit feedback for products they have actually purchased and allows the Admin/Owner to moderate submitted reviews. A review is associated with a specific purchased order item and includes a rating, an optional written comment, and up to three optional photos. Administrative moderation is manual; the owners may hide or unhide inappropriate feedback and record the reason for moderation. **Priority: Medium.**

### **4.18.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.18.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a registered customer views a completed purchase, the system identifies purchased items that are eligible for feedback.  
* When a customer attempts to review a product they did not purchase, the system prevents the feedback submission.  
* When a customer submits feedback for an eligible purchased item, the system records the rating and any optional comment or uploaded photos.  
* When a customer attempts to submit another review for the same purchased order item, the system prevents the duplicate feedback submission.  
* When a customer attaches review photos, the system accepts up to three images for that feedback entry.  
* When an Admin/Owner opens customer feedback, the system displays submitted feedback for administrative review.  
* When an Admin/Owner determines that a review is inappropriate, the owner hides the feedback and specifies the applicable moderation reason.  
* When an Admin/Owner restores previously hidden feedback, the system makes the feedback visible again.

### **4.18.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.18.3-functional-requirements}

## **4.19 Reports and Analytics** {#4.19-reports-and-analytics}

### **4.19.1 Description and Priority** {#4.19.1-description-and-priority}

This feature provides the Admin/Owner with a dashboard summarizing Kitchen406's transaction-derived business performance. The dashboard supports time-period filtering and presents sales performance, sales trends, product performance, and product-level cost and margin information. It is intended to provide straightforward operational and financial visibility based on the bakery's recorded data rather than advanced predictive analytics or forecasting. Financial analytics remain restricted to the Admin/Owner. **Priority: High.**

### **4.19.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.19.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an Admin/Owner opens the analytics dashboard, the system displays business-performance information derived from Kitchen406's recorded transactions.  
* When an Admin/Owner selects a time period, the system filters the applicable analytics views to the selected period.  
* When an Admin/Owner views sales performance, the system displays total sales and order volume for the selected period.  
* When an Admin/Owner views sales trends, the system displays how sales activity changes across relevant time periods, including recurring patterns such as differences by day of the week.  
* When an Admin/Owner views product performance, the system displays sales activity and order quantities by product.  
* When an Admin/Owner views product profitability information, the system displays available production-cost and margin information based on recipe, inventory, and pricing data.  
* When a Staff member attempts to access financial analytics, the system denies access to the restricted sales, cost, and profit information.

## **4.20 AI Marketing Assistant** {#4.20-ai-marketing-assistant}

### **4.20.1 Description and Priority** {#4.20.1-description-and-priority}

This feature uses Google's Gemini service to automatically generate draft Facebook marketing content using current data from the Kitchen406 platform. System events and weekly scheduled checks identify applicable marketing opportunities across the four supported categories. Each draft contains an AI-generated caption and image and is stored for Admin/Owner review. The owner retains full control by reviewing, editing, regenerating, approving, or rejecting generated content, and all actual Facebook publication remains manual and outside the system. **Priority: High.**

### **4.20.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.20.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a qualifying system event occurs or the weekly scheduled process runs, the system evaluates current Kitchen406 data for applicable marketing drafts.  
* When a predefined marketing condition is identified, the system compiles the relevant current business data and provides it as generation context to Gemini.  
* When a seasonal occasion becomes applicable, the system may use the configured occasion information as context for a seasonal marketing draft.  
* When Gemini successfully generates marketing content , the system stores the generated caption and image as a draft awaiting owner review.  
* When only the caption or image is generated successfully, the system stores the available content as an incomplete draft, identifies the missing content, and allows the Admin/Owner to retry generation for the missing component.  
* When an Admin/Owner opens a generated draft, the system displays its caption, image, category, and review information.  
* When an Admin/Owner edits the generated caption, the system saves the revised caption and records that the draft was edited.  
* When an Admin/Owner requests a replacement image, the system requests another image from Gemini and updates the draft's regeneration information.  
* When an Admin/Owner approves a draft, the system records the draft as approved and records the reviewing administrator.  
* When an Admin/Owner rejects a draft, the system records the draft as rejected.  
* When an approved draft is ready for use, the system does not publish it automatically; the owner manually posts the approved caption and image to Facebook.

# **5\. Other Nonfunctional Requirements** {#5.-other-nonfunctional-requirements}

## **5.1 Performance Requirements** {#5.1-performance-requirements}

* **NFR-PERF-01:** The system shall load customer-facing catalog and product pages within 3 seconds in at least 95% of test runs under the conditions specified in Chapter 4.7, excluding third-party service delays.

* **NFR-PERF-02:** The system shall complete ordinary internal operations, such as retrieving orders, inventory records, schedules, and dashboard information, within a target of 3 seconds under normal operating conditions, excluding third-party API latency.

* **NFR-PERF-03:** The system shall reflect a successfully confirmed PayMongo payment in the corresponding transaction and order records within a target of 5 seconds after receiving and verifying the applicable PayMongo webhook, excluding PayMongo's own webhook-delivery latency. PayMongo documents webhooks as its mechanism for real-time event notification and recommends webhook verification before processing.

* **NFR-PERF-04:** The system shall reflect a Lalamove delivery-status update within a target of 5 seconds after receiving the corresponding webhook, excluding latency before Lalamove delivers the webhook to the platform. Lalamove provides webhook-based order-status updates through API v3.

* **NFR-PERF-05:** The system shall initiate applicable email or SMS notification requests within a target of 5 seconds after the corresponding system event, excluding delivery time controlled by Brevo, Semaphore, mobile networks, or email providers.

* **NFR-PERF-06:** AI marketing draft generation shall execute asynchronously in the background so that Gemini response time does not block storefront, checkout, order-management, inventory, or dashboard operations.

* **NFR-PERF-07:** Capacity and inventory availability checks required during checkout shall complete before the customer is permitted to proceed with payment and shall not allow concurrent transactions to allocate the same unavailable capacity or stock.

## **5.2 Safety Requirements** {#5.2-safety-requirements}

For this system, safety mainly concerns preventing incorrect transactions, corrupted operational records, double allocation, and unintended automated actions, rather than physical safety.

* **NFR-SAF-01:** The system shall not confirm a standard order, activate a subscription, or finalize a custom-cake purchase unless the required payment has been successfully verified through PayMongo.

* **NFR-SAF-02:** The system shall reserve production capacity and required inventory for up to 32 minutes during QR Ph payment. At expiration, it shall verify payment status with PayMongo before confirming the order or releasing reservations. Late successful payments shall not automatically restore released reservations or confirm cancelled orders.

* **NFR-SAF-03:** The system shall process payment and other state-changing webhook events in a manner that prevents repeated delivery of the same event from creating duplicate orders, duplicate payments, duplicate reservations, or other duplicate state changes. PayMongo specifically recommends idempotent webhook handling because webhook delivery may be retried.

* **NFR-SAF-04:** Failures or temporary unavailability of PayMongo, Lalamove, Google Maps Platform, Brevo, Semaphore, Cloudinary, or Gemini shall not corrupt existing customer, order, inventory, capacity, payment, delivery, or marketing records.

* **NFR-SAF-05:** A failure of the AI marketing assistant shall not prevent customers or authorized personnel from using ordering, checkout, payment, inventory, scheduling, fulfillment, delivery, or analytics functions.

* **NFR-SAF-06:** Generated AI content shall remain in draft status until reviewed by an Admin/Owner and shall never cause automatic publication or changes to operational data.

* **NFR-SAF-07:** The system shall record critical application errors and failed external-service operations in server-side logs with sufficient information for diagnosis while excluding passwords, authentication secrets, and other sensitive credentials.

* **NFR-SAF-08:** If connectivity is lost while checkout or QR Ph payment is in progress, the system shall keep the transaction pending and unconfirmed. When connectivity is restored, the system shall check the existing payment session with PayMongo before offering another payment attempt, prevent duplicate order or payment processing, and display the current transaction status to the customer.

## **5.3 Security Requirements** {#5.3-security-requirements}

* **NFR-SEC-01**: The system shall transmit application data through HTTPS/TLS when communicating between clients, the platform, and supported external services.

* **NFR-SEC-02**: The system shall never store user passwords in plain text and shall protect them using an appropriate adaptive one-way password-hashing algorithm. OWASP recommends modern password-hashing algorithms such as configured bcrypt.

* **NFR-SEC-03**: The system shall enforce role-based authorization on the server side for Customer, Staff, and Admin/Owner accounts and shall deny access to functions or data not permitted for the authenticated user's role.

* **NFR-SEC-04**: The system shall ensure that customers may access only their own private profile, saved addresses, orders, subscriptions, custom cake requests, payments, deliveries, and other customer-specific transaction records.

* **NFR-SEC-05**: Authenticated sessions shall use secure session-management mechanisms and shall be invalidated when the user logs out or when the session expires. Session credentials shall not be exposed through URLs or insecure client-side storage. OWASP recommends server-side session expiration and appropriate protection of session identifiers.

* **NFR-SEC-06**: The system shall not store customers' banking credentials, e-wallet credentials, QR Ph authentication credentials, or other sensitive payment authentication information; payment authentication shall remain within PayMongo and the customer's supported banking or e-wallet environment.

* **NFR-SEC-07**: The system shall process personal information in accordance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173\) and shall provide appropriate transparency, legitimate-purpose limitations, proportional data collection, and reasonable organizational and technical safeguards.

* **NFR-SEC-08**: The system shall perform server-side validation of untrusted input and shall use appropriate output encoding and safe database-access mechanisms to reduce risks including malformed input, injection attacks, and cross-site scripting.

* **NFR-SEC-09**: Uploaded product images, custom-cake reference images, and review images shall be validated for permitted file type and size before being accepted for storage, and executable or unsupported file types shall be rejected.

* **NFR-SEC-10**: The system shall verify the Paymongo-Signature of incoming PayMongo webhooks before using them to change payment or order state. PayMongo documents HMAC-SHA256 signature verification using the webhook endpoint's secret.

* **NFR-SEC-11**: Server-side secrets, including PayMongo secret keys, Lalamove credentials, Gemini authentication credentials, Brevo and Semaphore API credentials, database credentials, and other private service secrets, shall be stored outside source code using protected environment configuration and shall not be exposed to client-side code. Vercel supports encrypted and sensitive environment variables for this purpose.

* **NFR-SEC-12**: Any Google Maps Platform API key that must be available to the web client shall be restricted to the authorized website and required Google Maps APIs. Server-side Maps credentials shall remain protected from client exposure. Google recommends both application and API restrictions for Maps keys.

* **NFR-SEC-13**: Server-side logs shall not record plaintext passwords, API secrets, payment authentication credentials, session tokens, or other secrets that are not necessary for diagnosis.

## **5.4 Software Quality Attributes** {#5.4-software-quality-attributes}

**Usability**

* **NFR-USE-01**: The system shall provide a responsive interface usable on supported desktop and mobile web browsers.

* **NFR-USE-02**: Customer-facing and administrative interfaces shall use clear and understandable labels, instructions, validation messages, and status descriptions suitable for non-technical users.

* **NFR-USE-03**: Forms shall identify invalid or missing information and provide the user with a clear indication of how to correct the problem.

* **NFR-USE-04**: Frequently performed customer tasks, including browsing products, managing a cart, checking out, viewing orders, and tracking deliveries, shall be accessible without unnecessary navigation or repeated data entry.

* **NFR-USE-05**: Core customer-facing interactions shall support keyboard navigation, descriptive input labels, visible keyboard focus, and accessible form validation feedback.

**Availability**

* **NFR-AVL-01**: The platform shall require an active internet connection and shall not provide an offline operating mode, consistent with its dependence on cloud hosting and external APIs.

* **NFR-AVL-02**: Failure of one nonessential external service shall not make unrelated platform functions unavailable where those functions can operate independently. For example, a Gemini outage shall not disable ordering or inventory functions, and an email/SMS failure shall not invalidate an otherwise confirmed order.

**Reliability**

* **NFR-REL-01**: The system shall handle unavailable, timed-out, rate-limited, or unsuccessful third-party API responses without corrupting existing platform data.

* **NFR-REL-02**: Where an external operation can safely be retried, the system shall preserve sufficient status information to permit retry without unintentionally creating duplicate transactions.

* **NFR-REL-03**: Payment, inventory-reservation, capacity-allocation, order, and delivery records shall remain internally consistent when a transaction fails partway through processing.

* **NFR-REL-04**: External-service errors shall present an appropriate user-facing message rather than exposing internal stack traces, credentials, or raw provider errors.

**Maintainability**

* **NFR-MNT-01**: The system shall maintain logical separation among customer-facing functionality, administrative functionality, staff operations, business logic, data access, and third-party integrations even though the application is implemented within a unified Next.js codebase.

* **NFR-MNT-02**: Third-party service credentials and environment-dependent configuration shall be externalized from source code.

* **NFR-MNT-03**: Functional and nonfunctional requirements shall retain unique identifiers to support traceability from requirements through implementation and testing.

* **NFR-MNT-04**: Configurable business values, including capacity baselines, cut-off rules, low-stock thresholds, markup, utility overhead, and applicable operational settings, shall not require source-code changes when modified through supported administrative configuration.

**Compatibility**

* **NFR-COMP-01**: The customer storefront, Admin/Owner interface, and Staff interface shall support the latest two major versions of Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and Apple Safari on applicable desktop and mobile platforms.

## **5.5 Business Rules** {#5.5-business-rules}

* **BR-01**: Guests may browse publicly available products and information, but a registered and authenticated customer account is required before placing a standard order, enrolling in a subscription, or submitting a custom cake request.

* **BR-02**: Kitchen406 supports three purchasing workflows only: Standard Orders, Prepaid Subscriptions, and Custom Cake Requests.

* **BR-03**: All supported purchases require full payment through QR Ph via PayMongo before the corresponding order or subscription is confirmed and committed to production.

* **BR-04**: QR Ph through PayMongo is the platform's sole supported payment method; direct card payments, separate e-wallet integrations, cash-on-delivery, and other payment gateways are outside the current system scope.

* **BR-05**: Discounts, vouchers, coupon codes, and promotional price reductions are not supported. Order totals consist of configured product prices and applicable fees. This matches the current scope limitation.

* **BR-06**: Same-day and rush fulfillment requests are not supported. Every purchasing workflow must satisfy its applicable minimum lead time and cut-off rules.

* **BR-07**: Production capacity for standard orders, subscriptions, and custom cakes shall be managed independently rather than drawn from one shared capacity pool.

* **BR-08**: The default standard-order capacity is a maximum of four product varieties per delivery day with up to ten units per variety, subject to Admin/Owner configuration.

* **BR-09**: The default subscription capacity is ten units per subscription product per week, subject to Admin/Owner configuration.

* **BR-10**: The default custom-cake capacity is two custom cakes per week, with each accepted cake assigned to a different fulfillment date, subject to Admin/Owner configuration.

* **BR-11**: A subscription is a prepaid commitment consisting of four scheduled weekly fulfillments and does not automatically renew or use recurring billing.

* **BR-12**: Each subscription consists of four scheduled weekly fulfillments associated with the customer's selected subscription schedule.

* **BR-13**: Each subscription permits one successful deferment, with rejected or ineligible requests excluded from the allowance. Successful deferments shall reschedule only the affected delivery while preserving its original scheduling record.

* **BR-14**: Inventory tracking is limited to single-level base ingredients. Prepared or intermediate components are not maintained as independent inventory items with nested Bills of Materials.

* **BR-15**: A product shall not remain orderable when a required ingredient is fully depleted and the order cannot be fulfilled from the available inventory.

* **BR-16**: The system-generated selling price is a recommendation only. The Admin/Owner retains final authority over the actual selling price.

* **BR-17**: Product costing is based on the applicable ingredient and packaging costs, configured utility overhead, and markup information maintained by the owners.

* **BR-18**: Custom-cake design and complexity pricing remains an Admin/Owner judgment. The system may calculate amounts associated with predefined cake options, but it shall not independently determine the final price of subjective design complexity.

* **BR-19**: Standard-order and subscription deliveries that use courier delivery shall be quoted, booked, and tracked through Lalamove. Each weekly subscription fulfillment is treated as its own order for courier purposes.

* **BR-20**: Custom cakes are delivered manually by the owners; the system shall not create or track Lalamove bookings for custom-cake delivery.

* **BR-21**: A customer may submit one review per eligible purchased order item, or one per subscription enrollment after all four weekly fulfillments have been completed. Individual subscription deliveries are not separately reviewable.

* **BR-22**: A customer review must contain a rating, an optional written comment, and up to three optional photos.

* **BR-23**: Customer-review moderation is performed manually by the Admin/Owner. The system does not perform automatic sentiment analysis, profanity classification, or automated dispute resolution.

* **BR-24**: Staff access is limited to authorized operational functions required for fulfillment, inventory work, schedules, recipes, and related notifications. Sensitive sales, profit, customer-management, pricing-configuration, analytics, and marketing-management functions remain restricted to the Admin/Owner.

* **BR-25**: The AI marketing assistant may use only the marketing-related operational context made available to it by the platform and shall have no authority to perform ordering, pricing, payment, inventory, delivery, or fulfillment decisions.

* **BR-26**: Marketing drafts are generated automatically through qualifying system events or weekly scheduled checks without requiring the Admin/Owner to initiate individual drafts.

* **BR-27**: Every AI-generated marketing item shall remain a draft until reviewed by an Admin/Owner. The owner may edit the caption, regenerate the image, approve the draft, or reject it.

* **BR-28**: Neither generated nor approved marketing content shall be automatically published to Facebook or another social-media platform. Actual publication remains a manual action performed by the owner.

* **BR-29**: The factual operational context supplied to Gemini, including applicable product, availability, subscription, and seasonal information, shall come from the current Kitchen406 system data rather than being invented as business facts by the model.

* **BR-30**: System outputs involving inventory, product costing, pricing suggestions, production capacity, and scheduling are dependent on the accuracy of the data maintained by the Admin/Owner and authorized Staff.

* **BR-31:** The delivery address selected for a subscription shall apply to all four fulfillments and remain unchanged after payment confirmation.

* **BR-32:** The delivery fees calculated during enrollment shall form part of the prepaid subscription total. Any differences between prepaid fees and actual courier charges at fulfillment shall be absorbed by the bakery without additional customer charges or refunds.

# **6\. Other Requirements** {#6.-other-requirements}

## **6.1 Data Privacy** {#6.1-data-privacy}

Kitchen406 shall process personal data in accordance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173\) and its Implementing Rules and Regulations. The system handles customer information such as names, email addresses, mobile numbers, saved delivery addresses, order and subscription records, custom cake information, review content and uploaded images, and payment-related transaction references. Personal data shall be collected only for legitimate purposes necessary to operate the platform and shall be protected using reasonable organizational and technical safeguards. Philippine privacy rules require transparency, legitimate purpose, proportionality, reasonable security measures, and retention only for as long as necessary.

| ID | Requirement Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| OR-PRIV-01 | The system shall collect and process only the personal information reasonably necessary to provide account, ordering, payment, delivery, notification, review, subscription, and custom-cake services. |
| OR-PRIV-02 | The system shall provide customers with an accessible privacy notice explaining what personal data is collected, why it is processed, how it is used, the relevant third-party recipients or service providers, and how customers may exercise their applicable privacy rights. |
| OR-PRIV-03 | The system shall process personal data only for declared and legitimate purposes related to Kitchen406's operations and shall not reuse the data for unrelated purposes without an appropriate lawful basis. |
| OR-PRIV-04 | The system shall not retain personal data longer than necessary for its declared purpose, legitimate business requirements, legal obligations, or the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims. |
| OR-PRIV-05 | The system shall provide an appropriate contact method through which customers may request access to or correction of their personal data and exercise other applicable rights provided under Philippine data-protection law. |
| OR-PRIV-06 | Personal data shared with external services such as PayMongo, Lalamove, Google Maps Platform, Brevo, Semaphore, Cloudinary, and other service providers shall be limited to information necessary for the corresponding service to operate. |
| OR-PRIV-07 | The AI marketing assistant shall not be provided with customer names, private contact information, delivery addresses, payment information, or other customer-specific personal data solely for the purpose of generating promotional content. |
| OR-PRIV-08 | Uploaded custom-cake reference images and customer-review images shall be treated as personal data when they contain identifiable individuals or other personal information and shall be protected accordingly. |
| OR-PRIV-09 | Access to customer personal data shall be restricted according to the user's authorized role and operational need. |
| OR-PRIV-10 | In the event of a personal-data breach requiring notification under applicable National Privacy Commission rules, Kitchen406 shall support the owners in complying with the required breach-notification procedures and time limits. The NPC generally requires notification within 72 hours for breaches meeting the applicable mandatory-reporting conditions. |

## **6.2 Localization** {#6.2-localization}

Kitchen406 Version 1.0 is intended exclusively for the Philippine market. The current SRS already defines Philippine Peso as the sole currency and identifies the platform as an internet-dependent Philippine-market system.

| ID | Requirement Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| OR-LOC-01 | The system shall use Philippine Peso (PHP) as the sole supported currency for product prices, order totals, delivery fees, custom-cake quotations, subscriptions, and analytics. |
| OR-LOC-02 | Monetary values displayed to users shall use the Philippine peso symbol or the PHP currency designation where appropriate. |
| OR-LOC-03 | The system shall use English as the supported interface language for Version 1.0. Filipino and other language localizations are outside the current scope. |
| OR-LOC-04 | Dates, fulfillment schedules, cut-off times, subscription schedules, and other time-dependent operations shall use Philippine local time, Asia/Manila (UTC+08:00). |
| OR-LOC-05 | Customer mobile numbers used for SMS notifications shall support valid Philippine mobile-number formats compatible with the configured SMS provider. |
| OR-LOC-06 | The system shall not provide foreign-currency conversion or international market localization in Version 1.0. |

## **6.3 Regulatory Requirements** {#6.3-regulatory-requirements}

Because Kitchen406 will accept live online transactions through its own website, the deployed platform falls within Philippine rules governing e-commerce and consumer transactions. Republic Act No. 11967, the Internet Transactions Act of 2023, applies to business-to-consumer internet transactions in the Philippines and establishes obligations for e-retailers, including business disclosure, consumer redress, privacy protection, and the issuance of receipts or invoices. Its Implementing Rules and Regulations were adopted on May 24, 2024\. This section distinguishes responsibilities as follows: the system provides the storefront and transaction functions specified in this section; the owners supply accurate business information and maintain the registrations, tax compliance, permits, and licenses applicable to Kitchen406; and PayMongo provides the payment-processing infrastructure used by the platform. These allocations describe the project’s responsibilities and do not by themselves certify legal compliance.

| ID | Requirement Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| OR-REG-01 | The deployed system shall comply with applicable provisions of the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173\) and relevant issuances of the National Privacy Commission when processing customer personal data. |
| OR-REG-02 | The deployed storefront shall comply with applicable requirements of the Internet Transactions Act of 2023 (RA 11967\) and its Implementing Rules and Regulations for business-to-consumer internet transactions. |
| OR-REG-03 | The storefront shall display the Kitchen406 business or trade name, the legally applicable business address, and customer contact information required of an e-retailer. The owners shall be responsible for supplying accurate and legally publishable business information. |
| OR-REG-04 | Products offered through the storefront shall display clear and accurate product information and the applicable selling price before purchase. Philippine consumer law requires retail prices to be clearly displayed and prohibits deceptive representations. |
| OR-REG-05 | The system shall provide or make available an appropriate electronic receipt or invoice for completed online sales in accordance with applicable legal and tax requirements. RA 11967 requires e-retailers and online merchants to issue paper or electronic invoices or receipts for sales. |
| OR-REG-06 | The deployed storefront shall provide an accessible customer-support or complaint channel that serves as Kitchen406's internal redress mechanism. This requirement does not require development of a full customer-support ticketing system if an accessible and functional contact mechanism satisfies the business's implementation. |
| OR-REG-07 | QR-based payments shall use QR Ph through PayMongo rather than a proprietary payment QR implementation. BSP Circular No. 1055 established the national QR-code standard, while the payment service provider is responsible for the regulated payment-processing infrastructure. |
| OR-REG-08 | Customer-facing policies shall not remove or limit remedies that customers are entitled to under applicable Philippine consumer-protection laws when loss, defect, non-delivery, or another problem occurs without the customer's fault. |
| OR-REG-09 | Business registration, taxation compliance, food-business permits, sanitary permits, and other licenses required for Kitchen406's legal operation shall remain the responsibility of the business owners and are outside the software's responsibility to obtain or validate. |

## **6.4 Customer-Facing Policies** {#6.4-customer-facing-policies}

The following policies shall be communicated clearly to customers through the storefront and the relevant transaction flow. Applicable policies shall be accessible before the customer commits to a purchase, subscription, or other paid transaction.

| ID | Requirement Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| OR-POL-01 | The system shall make the current customer-facing policies reasonably accessible from the customer storefront. |
| OR-POL-02 | The system shall present or link the policies relevant to a transaction before the customer completes the corresponding purchase or subscription enrollment. |
| OR-POL-03 | Customers shall be responsible for providing accurate contact information, delivery information, and other transaction details required for fulfillment. |
| OR-POL-04 | A standard order, subscription enrollment, or finalized custom-cake order shall not be considered confirmed until the required full payment has been successfully processed through PayMongo. |
| OR-POL-05 | Requested fulfillment dates remain subject to the applicable lead-time, cut-off, blocked-date, inventory, and production-capacity rules of Kitchen406. |
| OR-POL-06 | Same-day and rush fulfillment shall not be available through the platform. |
| OR-POL-07 | Customers selecting delivery shall be responsible for providing a valid serviceable delivery address and for remaining reasonably available through the contact information provided for fulfillment of the order. |
| OR-POL-08 | When an order cannot be received or collected solely because of the customer's action or inaction, such as the customer's unavailability, refusal to receive an otherwise valid order, failure to appear for an agreed pickup, or incorrect customer-provided delivery or contact information, the order may be considered forfeited and Kitchen406 shall not be required to perform another delivery or fulfillment attempt. Customers may dispute a forfeiture by contacting Kitchen406 through its existing customer support channels.The Admin/Owner shall review and resolve such disputes manually on a case-by-case basis. |
| OR-POL-09 | The forfeiture policy shall not apply when failure to complete fulfillment results from Kitchen406, the courier, a system failure, or another circumstance not attributable to the customer. Nothing in this policy shall remove any remedy that must be provided to the customer under applicable law. This limitation is important because Philippine e-commerce law preserves consumer remedies where loss or nonconformity occurs without the consumer's fault. |
| OR-POL-10 | A Kitchen406 subscription shall consist of a prepaid commitment consisting of four scheduled weekly fulfillments and shall not automatically renew. |
| OR-POL-11 | Each subscription permits one deferment that the system successfully applies. Rejected or ineligible requests shall not consume the allowance. |
| OR-POL-12 | Customers shall submit deferment requests before the affected fulfillment’s preparation day begins. The system shall check only two replacement dates: the next day and one week after the subscription’s final scheduled fulfillment. It shall offer only dates with sufficient production capacity. |
| OR-POL-13 | If the customer confirms an offered date and the allowance is unused, the system shall apply the deferment automatically without manual Admin/Owner approval. If neither replacement date has sufficient capacity, the request is late, or the allowance has been used, the system shall reject the request, preserve the original schedule, and leave the allowance unused.  |
| OR-POL-14 | Submission of a custom-cake request shall not guarantee acceptance of the request. The Admin/Owner retains responsibility for determining whether the requested design, schedule, and requirements can reasonably be fulfilled. |
| OR-POL-15 | A custom-cake order shall proceed to confirmed production only after the customer accepts the applicable final quotation and completes the required payment. |
| OR-POL-16 | Custom-cake delivery shall be handled directly by the Kitchen406 owners and shall not use the platform's Lalamove booking workflow. |
| OR-POL-17 | Customers may submit a review only for an eligible item that they purchased through a completed order, subject to the review requirements defined by the system. |
| OR-POL-18 | Kitchen406 may hide customer reviews containing spam, abusive language, off-topic material, sexual content, or other content determined to be inappropriate under the platform's moderation rules. |
| OR-POL-19 | Customer-facing policies shall be written in clear language and shall not contain terms intended to waive mandatory rights granted to customers under Philippine law. |
| OR-POL-20 | Customers must confirm their subscription delivery address before payment, as it cannot be changed after enrollment. |

**Appendix A: Glossary**

| Term | Definition |
| ----- | ----- |
| Admin / Owner | A Kitchen406 business owner with administrative access to management functions such as products, pricing, orders, inventory, capacity, analytics, staff accounts, customer feedback, and AI marketing drafts. |
| AI Marketing Assistant | The system feature that uses Gemini to automatically create promotional caption-and-image drafts using current Kitchen406 business information for later owner review. |
| API (Application Programming Interface) | A way for Kitchen406 to communicate with an external software service such as PayMongo, Lalamove, Brevo, Semaphore, Google Maps Platform, or Gemini. |
| Bill of Materials (BoM) | The recipe-based list of raw ingredients and required quantities needed to produce a particular product variation or configurable cake component. |
| Blocked Date | A date configured by the Admin/Owner on which the system does not allow new applicable bookings or fulfillment commitments. |
| Brevo | The external service used by Kitchen406 to send applicable email notifications to customers. |
| Capacity Allocation | Production capacity assigned to a particular order, subscription fulfillment, or custom cake for its scheduled fulfillment period. |
| Capacity Limit | The maximum amount of work Kitchen406 allows to be scheduled for a particular order type and time period. |
| Checkout | The stage in which a registered customer reviews the transaction, selects applicable fulfillment information, passes capacity and inventory checks, and completes payment. |
| Checkout Hold | A temporary 32-minute reservation of production capacity and required inventory during checkout, including a two-minute allowance beyond the 30-minute QR Ph payment session.  |
| Cloudinary | The external cloud service used to store image files such as product images, custom-cake reference images, customer-review photos, and generated marketing images. |
| Cost-Based Pricing | A pricing method in which the system calculates production cost from recipe and cost information and applies a configured markup to produce a suggested selling price. |
| Customer | A registered user who can perform transactions such as placing standard orders, enrolling in subscriptions, submitting custom cake requests, making payments, tracking orders, and providing feedback. |
| Customer-Facing Policy | A business rule or condition that must be communicated to customers, such as fulfillment, deferment, payment, delivery, or order-forfeiture conditions. |
| Custom Cake Request | A customer request for a personalized cake using configurable options and add-ons that must be reviewed by the Admin/Owner before a final quotation and purchase can proceed. |
| Cut-off Time | The latest permitted time for a customer to make an applicable booking or transaction for a particular fulfillment schedule. |
| Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173\) | The Philippine law governing the collection, processing, protection, and handling of personal information. |
| Deferment | A customer-requested rescheduling of one upcoming subscription fulfillment. Each subscription permits one deferment. The customer must request it before the affected fulfillment’s preparation day begins. The system checks only the next day and one week after the final scheduled fulfillment, offers dates with sufficient production capacity, and applies the customer-confirmed choice automatically. If neither date has capacity or the request is otherwise ineligible, it is rejected without consuming the allowance. The subscription still has four fulfillments; an applied deferment may extend the calendar end date. |
| Delivery Status | The latest delivery-progress state received by Kitchen406 from Lalamove after a courier booking has been created. |
| Final Selling Price | The actual product price selected and approved by the Admin/Owner and charged to customers. It is stored separately from the system-generated suggested price. |
| Forfeited Order | An order for which no additional fulfillment attempt is required because the customer failed to receive or collect it due to the customer's own action or inaction, subject to the customer-facing policies and applicable law. |
| Fulfillment | The process of preparing and completing a confirmed customer order through either pickup or the applicable delivery arrangement. |
| Fulfillment Date | The scheduled date on which an order or subscription delivery is expected to be completed for the customer. |
| Fulfillment Method | The method through which an applicable order is received by the customer, such as pickup or delivery. |
| Gemini | Google's generative AI service used by Kitchen406 only for generating marketing captions and accompanying images. |
| Google Maps Platform | The external location service used to validate delivery addresses, display or confirm locations, calculate routes or distances, and determine whether an address is within the bakery's serviceable area. |
| Guest | An unauthenticated visitor who may browse publicly available products and information but cannot complete customer transactions. |
| Ingredient Inventory | The recorded quantities of raw ingredients currently maintained by Kitchen406 for production and material planning. |
| Inventory Adjustment | A manual change to recorded ingredient stock made to correct differences caused by situations such as spoilage, damage, miscounts, theft, or corrections. |
| Inventory Movement | A recorded change in actual ingredient stock resulting from activities such as consumption, restocking, reversal, or manual adjustment. |
| Inventory Reservation | An ingredient quantity set aside for a pending or confirmed transaction so that the same available stock is not committed to another order. |
| Internet Transactions Act of 2023 (RA 11967\) | The Philippine law governing internet-based commercial transactions and applicable obligations of online businesses and consumers. |
| Lalamove | The third-party courier service integrated with Kitchen406 for delivery quotations, courier booking, and delivery-status tracking for supported standard orders and subscription fulfillments. |
| Lead Time | The minimum amount of advance time required between placing or confirming a transaction and its requested fulfillment date. |
| Low-Stock Threshold | A configured stock level at which the system alerts the Admin/Owner that an ingredient may require replenishment. |
| Manual Publication | The requirement that an Admin/Owner personally posts approved AI-generated marketing content to Facebook or another platform rather than Kitchen406 publishing it automatically. |
| Markup Percentage | The configurable percentage applied to calculated production cost to produce the system's suggested selling price. |
| Marketing Draft | A generated promotional caption-and-image pair stored in Kitchen406 for Admin/Owner review, editing, regeneration, approval, or rejection before any manual publication. |
| Material Requirement | The quantity of an ingredient that the system determines is needed to fulfill a particular pending or confirmed order based on its recipe or configuration. |
| Notification Log | A system record of an outgoing customer notification, including information such as its type, recipient context, provider, sending status, retry information, and related activity. |
| PayMongo | The external payment service used by Kitchen406 to process and confirm QR Ph payments. |
| Personal Data | Information relating to an identifiable person that is collected or processed by the system, such as customer contact details, addresses, transaction records, and certain uploaded content. |
| Product Margin | The estimated percentage of a product's selling price remaining after deducting its estimated production cost, excluding delivery, marketing, and other unaccounted expenses; it does not represent actual net profit. |
| Product Variant | A specific sellable version of a product, such as a particular product size, which may have its own price and Bill of Materials. |
| Production Capacity | The amount of production work Kitchen406 is configured to accept for a particular purchasing workflow and scheduling period. |
| QR Ph | The Philippine national interoperable QR payment standard used by Kitchen406 through PayMongo for online payment. |
| Quotation | A price and set of agreed fulfillment details issued by the Admin/Owner for a custom cake request for the customer's review and acceptance. |
| Recipe | The ingredient and quantity information associated with a product variation and used by the system for production, inventory planning, and costing. |
| Review / Customer Feedback | A rating submitted for a product from a customer's completed purchase, optionally accompanied by written comments and up to three photos. |
| Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) | The system's method of restricting features and information according to whether the authenticated user is a Customer, Staff member, or Admin/Owner. |
| Seasonal Occasion | An Admin/Owner-managed event or date period that may be used as context when generating seasonal marketing drafts. |
| Semaphore | The external SMS gateway used by Kitchen406 to send applicable text-message notifications to customers. |
| Serviceable Area | The geographic area within which Kitchen406 accepts supported delivery orders, determined using the selected delivery address and location services. |
| Single-Level BoM | Kitchen406's Bill of Materials structure in which finished products are linked directly to base ingredients without separately tracking intermediate or prepared components with their own BoMs. |
| Staff | An account created and controlled by the Admin/Owner for bakery personnel who perform authorized operational tasks such as fulfillment, inventory work, recipe viewing, scheduling, and related status updates. |
| Standard Order | A normal customer purchase of products and product variations listed in the Kitchen406 storefront at their configured selling prices. |
| Subscription | A prepaid, non-auto-renewing Kitchen406 arrangement consisting of one eligible product delivered once per week over a four-week cycle. |
| Subscription Fulfillment | One of the individual weekly deliveries that make up a customer's four-week subscription. Each fulfillment is scheduled and handled separately. |
| Suggested Selling Price | A price calculated by the system from production cost and the configured markup percentage for the Admin/Owner's consideration. It does not automatically become the product's final selling price. |
| System Notification | An internal notification displayed within Kitchen406 to an authorized Admin/Owner or Staff member concerning an operational event relevant to that user's role. |
| Utility Overhead | An owner-configured amount representing production expenses such as gas and electricity that is included when calculating a product's production cost. |
| Webhook | An automated message sent from an external service to Kitchen406 when an event occurs, such as PayMongo reporting a payment result or Lalamove reporting a delivery-status change. |
